title: Approaches to Learning
source_text: Approaches to Learning

title: Motivation to Learn
source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Motivation to Learn

title: Curiosity and Interest
source_text: Sub-Strand — Curiosity and Interest

title: Curiosity and Interest
description: Express interest in some familiar and new objects, people, and activities in their immediate environment. Seek information by exploring with their senses, describing their observations, and asking simple questions.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Curiosity and Interest
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Express interest in some familiar and new objects, people, and activities in their immediate environment. Seek information by exploring with their senses, describing their observations, and asking simple questions.

title: Curiosity and Interest
description: Express interest in a broader range of familiar and new objects, people, and activities by exploring more extensively with their senses, describing their observations in greater detail, and asking more detailed questions.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Curiosity and Interest
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Express interest in a broader range of familiar and new objects, people, and activities by exploring more extensively with their senses, describing their observations in greater detail, and asking more detailed questions.

title: Initiative
source_text: Sub-Strand - Initiative

title: Initiative
description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as simple play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others), and seeking solutions to problems.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Initiative
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as simple play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others), and seeking solutions to problems.

title: Initiative
description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as detailed and more complex play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others) more often, and seeking solutions to problems more persistently.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Initiative
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as detailed and more complex play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others) more often, and seeking solutions to problems more persistently.

title: Engagement
source_text: Sub-Strand — Engagement

title: Engagement
description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for brief periods of time with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Engagement
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for brief periods of time with adult support.

title: Engagement
description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for longer periods of time with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Engagement
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for longer periods of time with less adult support.

title: Perseverance
source_text: Sub-Strand — Perseverance

title: Persisting Despite Difficulties
description: Demonstrate persistence, with adult support, when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. Make an effort, with adult support, to cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, anger, sadness, excitement), although may shift to another activity after a short while.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Persisting Despite Difficulties
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate persistence, with adult support, when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. Make an effort, with adult support, to cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, anger, sadness, excitement), although may shift to another activity after a short while.

title: Persisting Despite Difficulties
description: Demonstrate persistence for longer periods of time when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. More consistently cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, sadness, anger, excitement) and can continue engaging in an activity with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Persisting Despite Difficulties
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Demonstrate persistence for longer periods of time when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. More consistently cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, sadness, anger, excitement) and can continue engaging in an activity with less adult support.

title: Executive Functioning
source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Executive Functioning

title: Working Memory
source_text: Sub-Strand - Working Memory

title: Working Memory
description: Hold approximately one to two pieces of information in their mind for a short time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when performing tasks and engaging in play, with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Working Memory
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Hold approximately one to two pieces of information in their mind for a short time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when performing tasks and engaging in play, with adult support.

title: Working Memory
description: Hold approximately two to three pieces of information in their mind for longer periods of time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when engaging in multistep tasks and more complex play, with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Working Memory
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Hold approximately two to three pieces of information in their mind for longer periods of time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when engaging in multistep tasks and more complex play, with less adult support.

title: Inhibitory Control
source_text: Sub-Strand — Inhibitory Control

title: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
description: Demonstrate emerging ability to manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Managing Impulsive Behaviors
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with adult support.

title: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
description: Manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Managing Impulsive Behaviors
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with less adult support.

title: Managing Attention and Distractions
description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities; however, often need adult support to manage attention when distracted or interrupted.
source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Managing Attention and Distractions
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities; however, often need adult support to manage attention when distracted or interrupted.

title: Managing Attention and Distractions
description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Managing Attention and Distractions
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities with less adult support.

title: Flexibility
source_text: Sub-Strand - Flexibility

title: Flexibility
description: Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.4 Flexibility
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with adult support.

title: Flexibility
description: More consistently shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 2.4 Flexibility
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
More consistently shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with less adult support.

title: Goal-Directed Learning
source_text: Strand: 3.0 — Goal-Directed Learning

title: Problem-Solving
source_text: Sub-Strand - Problem-Solving

title: Planning
description: Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry out simple goals (for example, one- to two-step plans and goals), with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 3.1 Planning
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry out simple goals (for example, one- to two-step plans and goals), with adult support.

title: Planning
description: Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more complex plans (for example, two- to three-step plans and goals), with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 3.1 Planning
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more complex plans (for example, two- to three-step plans and goals), with less adult support.

title: Reflecting and Analyzing
description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 3.2 Reflecting and Analyzing
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with adult support.

title: Reflecting and Analyzing
description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 3.2 Reflecting and Analyzing
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with less adult support.

title: Collaborative Effort
source_text: Sub-Strand - - Collaborative Effort

title: Problem-Solving Together
description: Collaborate with peers in problem-solving during play and learning activities, sometimes for a short period of time and sometimes longer.
source_text:
Foundation 3.3 Problem-Solving Together
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Collaborate with peers in problem-solving during play and learning activities, sometimes for a short period of time and sometimes longer.

title: Problem-Solving Together
description: Engage in extended collaborative problem-solving during play and learning activities. Communicate with peers about how to solve a problem and help peers when needed.
source_text:
Foundation 3.3 Problem-Solving Together
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Engage in extended collaborative problem-solving during play and learning activities. Communicate with peers about how to solve a problem and help peers when needed.

title: Understanding Others
description: Notice, with adult support, that others have different approaches and preferences, although often have difficulty accepting others' approaches or preferences.
source_text:
Foundation 3.4 Understanding Others
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Notice, with adult support, that others have different approaches and preferences, although often have difficulty accepting others' approaches or preferences.

title: Understanding Others
description: Demonstrate understanding and explain that others can have different approaches and preferences and more consistently accept others' approaches and preferences, with less adult support.
source_text:
Foundation 3.4 Understanding Others
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate understanding and explain that others can have different approaches and preferences and more consistently accept others' approaches and preferences, with less adult support.

title: Foundational Language Development
description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.
source_text:
Foundational Language Development
This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

title: Listening and Speaking
source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Listening and Speaking

title: Vocabulary
source_text: Sub-Strand - Vocabulary

title: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
description: Understand and use words for objects, actions, and attributes frequently experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding and Using Vocabulary
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Understand and use words for objects, actions, and attributes frequently experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

title: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
description: Understand and use an increasing variety of words for objects, actions, and attributes experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding and Using Vocabulary
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Understand and use an increasing variety of words for objects, actions, and attributes experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

title: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
description: Understand and use commonly experienced vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Understanding and Using Words for Categories
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Understand and use commonly experienced vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

title: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
description: Understand and use increasingly specific vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Understanding and Using Words for Categories
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Understand and use increasingly specific vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

title: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
description: Understand and use words to describe the size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and "on"), including simple comparisons (such as "bigger").
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Understand and use words to describe the size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and "on"), including simple comparisons (such as "bigger").

title: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
description: Understand and use increasingly specific words to describe and compare the size and location of objects (such as "longer" and "between").
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Understand and use increasingly specific words to describe and compare the size and location of objects (such as "longer" and "between").

title: Grammar
source_text: Sub-Strand - Grammar

title: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
description: Use common word forms and sentence forms to express thoughts and ideas.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure*
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use common word forms and sentence forms to express thoughts and ideas.

title: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
description: Use both common and less common word forms and sentence forms to express complex thoughts and ideas.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure*
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Use both common and less common word forms and sentence forms to express complex thoughts and ideas.

title: Asking Questions
description: Use questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.
source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Asking Questions
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

title: Asking Questions
description: Use questions and follow-up questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.
source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Asking Questions
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Use questions and follow-up questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

title: Constructing Narratives
description: Use language to construct real or fictional short narratives.
source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Constructing Narratives
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use language to construct real or fictional short narratives.

title: Constructing Narratives
description: Use language to construct real or fictional extended narratives that have several details or a plotline.
source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Constructing Narratives
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Use language to construct real or fictional extended narratives that have several details or a plotline.

title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
description: Share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Share descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
description: Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

title: Participating in Conversations
description: Participate in back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at least one turn in a conversation.
source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Participate in back-and-forth conversations
with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at
least one turn in a conversation.

title: Participating in Conversations
description: Participate in increasingly long and complex back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic across several turns in the conversation.
source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Participate in increasingly long and complex
back-and-forth conversations with adults and
peers. Respond on topic across several turns
in the conversation.

title: Foundational Literacy Skills
source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Foundational Literacy Skills

title: Phonological Awareness
source_text: Sub-Strand — Phonological Awareness

title: Isolating Initial Sounds
description: Match words that have the same first sound in speech, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Match words that have the same first sound in
speech, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

title: Isolating Initial Sounds
description: Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a word, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a
word, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
description: When presented with two single-syllable words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them into a compound word in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
When presented with two single-syllable
words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them
into a compound word in speech with adult
support or the support of pictures or objects.

title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
description: When presented with syllables and individual sounds, blend them into words in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
When presented with syllables and individual
sounds, blend them into words in speech with
adult support or the support of pictures or
objects.

title: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
description: Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or songs.
source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or
songs.

title: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
description: Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense words.
source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes
may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense
words.

title: English Language Development
description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.
source_text:
English Language Development
This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

title: Listening and Speaking
source_text: Strand: 1.0 — Listening and Speaking

title: Vocabulary
source_text: Sub-Strand — Vocabulary

title: Understanding Words
description: Pay attention to English oral language and understand a few common English words, while relying mainly on intonation, facial expressions, and gestures of the speaker in interactions with adults and peers.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Discovering
Pay attention to English oral
language and understand
a few common English
words, while relying
mainly on intonation, facial
expressions, and gestures of
the speaker in interactions
with adults and peers.

title: Understanding Words
description: Demonstrate understanding of words in English for objects and actions as well as phrases encountered frequently in interactions with adults and peers.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Developing
Demonstrate understanding
of words in English for
objects and actions as well
as phrases encountered
frequently in interactions
with adults and peers.

title: Understanding Words
description: Demonstrate understanding of a larger set of words in English (for example, objects and actions, personal pronouns, possessives, and descriptive terms) in interactions with adults and peers.
source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Broadening
Demonstrate understanding
of a larger set of words
in English (for example,
objects and actions, personal
pronouns, possessives,
and descriptive terms) in
interactions with adults and
peers.

title: Using Words
description: Use English words, mainly consisting of concrete nouns.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Discovering
Use English words, mainly
consisting of concrete nouns.

title: Using Words
description: Use varied English words, including an increasing number of concrete nouns and some verbs and pronouns.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Developing
Use varied English words,
including an increasing
number of concrete nouns
and some verbs and
pronouns.

title: Using Words
description: Use a wide variety of English words to share knowledge of concepts, including words across all parts of speech, with some inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Broadening
Use a wide variety of English
words to share knowledge
of concepts, including words
across all parts of speech,
with some inaccuracies.

title: Grammar
source_text: Sub-Strand — Grammar

title: Using Grammatical Features
description: Use one or two familiar English verbs as all-purpose verbs, with some inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Discovering
Use one or two familiar
English verbs as all-
purpose verbs, with some
inaccuracies.

title: Using Grammatical Features
description: Use some grammatical rules in English, such as using -S or -es for plural nouns and -ing for verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Developing
Use some grammatical rules
in English, such as using -S or
-es for plural nouns and -ing
for verbs, sometimes with
inaccuracies.

title: Using Grammatical Features
description: Broaden the use of English grammatical rules, such as irregular plurals or simple past tense verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Broadening
Broaden the use of English
grammatical rules, such as
irregular plurals or simple
past tense verbs, sometimes
with inaccuracies.

title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
description: Use words or phrases repeatedly experienced in English to communicate.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Discovering
Use words or phrases
repeatedly experienced in
English to communicate.

title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
description: Use a few formulaic English grammatical forms, with some inaccuracies, to produce many different types of sentence structures.
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Developing
Use a few formulaic English
grammatical forms, with
some inaccuracies, to
produce many different
types of sentence structures.

title: Using Complex Sentence Structures
description: Use a variety of English sentence structures to communicate on a range of topics by switching out key words in a phrase. Grammatical forms can include adding appropriate possessive pronouns (for example, your, my); conjunctions (for example, and, or); and other elements (for example, adjectives, adverbs).
source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Broadening
Use a variety of English
sentence structures to
communicate on a range of
topics by switching out key
words in a phrase.
Grammatical forms can
include adding appropriate
possessive pronouns
(for example, your, my);
conjunctions (for example,
and, or); and other elements
(for example, adjectives,
adverbs).

title: Language Use
source_text: Sub-Strand — Language Use

title: Communicating Needs
description: Combine nonverbal communication and some English phrases to be understood by English speakers.
source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Discovering
Combine nonverbal
communication and some
English phrases to be
understood by English
speakers.

title: Communicating Needs
description: Use single English words and nonverbal communication with English speakers, such as gestures or behaviors, to seek attention, make a request, or initiate a response.
source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Developing
Use single English words and
nonverbal communication
with English speakers, such
as gestures or behaviors,
to seek attention, make
a request, or initiate a
response.

title: Communicating Needs
description: Show increasing reliance on verbal communication in English to be understood by English speakers.
source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Broadening
Show increasing reliance on
verbal communication in
English to be understood by
English speakers.

title: Understanding Requests and Directions
description: Follow simple directions in English that involve repeatedly experienced routines or contextual clues.
source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Discovering
Follow simple directions
in English that involve repeatedly
experienced routines or
contextual clues.

title: Understanding Requests and Directions
description: Follow directions in English when given additional contextual clues.
source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Developing
Follow directions in English
when given
additional contextual clues.

title: Understanding Requests and Directions
description: Follow directions that involve more than one step, relying less on contextual clues.
source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Broadening
Follow directions that involve
more than one step, relying
less on contextual clues.

title: Asking Questions
description: Use a few question structures as a formula, filling in different words to ask about various topics.
source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Discovering
Use a few question
structures as a formula,
filling in different words to
ask about various topics.

title: Asking Questions
description: Use a frequently experienced question phrase (such as "What's that?") or use one or two English words with a rising pitch to ask questions.
source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Developing
Use a frequently experienced
question phrase (such as
"What's that?") or use one
or two English words with a
rising pitch to ask questions.

title: Asking Questions
description: Use "who," "what," "why," "how," "when," and "where" to produce questions in many forms to ask about a variety of topics in English.
source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Broadening
Use "who," "what," "why,"
"how," "when," and "where"
to produce questions in
many forms to ask about a
variety of topics in English.

title: Constructing Narratives
description: Identify parts of real or fictional narratives using a few English vocabulary words.
source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Discovering
Identify parts of real or
fictional narratives using
a few English vocabulary
words.

title: Constructing Narratives
description: Construct real or fictional short narratives using English vocabulary in a few simple English sentence structures.
source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Developing
Construct real or fictional
short narratives using English
vocabulary in a few simple
English sentence structures.

title: Constructing Narratives
description: Construct real or fictional narratives by stringing together sentences with varied structures in English.
source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Constructing Narratives
Broadening
Construct real or fictional
narratives by stringing
together sentences with
varied structures in English.

title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
description: Use English vocabulary and gestures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Discovering
Use English vocabulary
and gestures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
description: Use a few simple sentence structures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Developing
Use a few simple sentence
structures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

title: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
description: Use varied sentence structures to share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.
source_text:
Foundation 1.9 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Broadening
Use varied sentence
structures to share
descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

title: Participating in Conversations
description: Engage in conversations in English speakers, by mostly listening and responding with a few English words, gestures, or other nonverbal responses.
source_text:
Foundation 1.10 Participating in Conversations
Discovering
Engage in conversations in English speakers, by mostly listening and responding with a few English words, gestures, or other nonverbal responses.

title: Participating in Conversations
description: Converse with others using frequently heard vocabulary in English, often using short, commonly used sentences and phrases and a few repeated grammatical structures, sometimes with inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.10 Participating in Conversations
Developing
Converse with others using frequently heard vocabulary in English, often using short, commonly used sentences and phrases and a few repeated grammatical structures, sometimes with inaccuracies.

title: Participating in Conversations
description: Engage in conversation with English using increasingly complex vocabulary and varied grammatical structures, sometimes with inaccuracies.
source_text:
Foundation 1.10 Participating in Conversations
Broadening
Engage in conversation with English using increasingly complex vocabulary and varied grammatical structures, sometimes with inaccuracies.

title: Foundational Literacy Skills
source_text: Strand: 2.0 — Foundational Literacy Skills

title: Phonological Awareness
source_text: Sub-Strand - Phonological Awareness

title: Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
description: Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
Discovering
Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.

title: Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
description: Match English words that have the same first sound in speech, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
Developing
Match English words that have the same first sound in speech, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

title: Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
description: Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a word in English, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.
source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Recognizing and Segmenting Sounds
Broadening
Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a word in English, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
description: Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.
source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds
Discovering
Recognize and produce sounds of spoken English.

title: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
